section_summary: This section concerns the Allied-controlled Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition of 1946–47: its authorization, route, observers, expected food and oil production, and objections from Australia and Norway. It also contains SCAP directives, fleet status and coastal catch reports, correspondence about the International Whaling Conference, and a brief unrelated exchange about Japanese cultured pearls.

subfiles.title: Australian aide-mémoire on Japanese Antarctic whaling
subfiles.about: Australia accepts an inspector position while protesting the expedition and seeking consultation, route details, and reparations.
subfiles.summary: Australia lists eight U.S. assurances about the expedition. It objects to future Japanese Antarctic whaling, asks for a share of whaling equipment as reparations and the fleet's route, and argues that SCAP should have consulted the Allied Council before issuing its August order.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Australian aide-mémoire
subfiles.about: The United States confirms its assurances and supplies information on the fleet, route, and halted tanker conversion.
subfiles.summary: The Department welcomes Australia's inspector and confirms the eight assurances while declining to commit on future Japanese whaling. It says conversion of a third tanker has stopped and reparations require international agreement. SCAP's account describes fleet departures and the route through the Celebes Sea and Lombok Strait.

subfiles.title: Telegram concerning Australian whaling inspectors
subfiles.about: A badly degraded telegram concerns arrangements for Australian inspectors joining the Japanese whaling expedition.
subfiles.summary: The legible text concerns Australian inspector travel and supplies.

subfiles.title: Passage through Lombok Strait approved
subfiles.about: Batavia reports approval for the Japanese whaling fleet to pass through Lombok Strait.
subfiles.summary: The Netherlands mission in Tokyo was informed of the approval.

subfiles.title: Document charge slip
subfiles.about: A State Department form records a file charge.
subfiles.summary: Charge slip for a whaling file item.

subfiles.title: Weekly report on Japanese whaling: covering despatch
subfiles.about: The Political Adviser forwards SCAPIN 1321 appointing U.S. Army representatives to the Antarctic fleet.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the order naming Terry and McCracken as SCAP representatives.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1321: representatives with the whaling fleet
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: SCAP appoints Terry and McCracken to supervise compliance aboard the fleet.
subfiles.summary: Names two Army officers and requires Japanese assistance and radio access.

subfiles.title: Letter about availability of Japanese cultured pearls
subfiles.about: Gross responds to a request about when Japanese pearls will be available.
subfiles.summary: Pearls appear unlikely to be available until late 1947.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Japanese cultured pearls
subfiles.about: A memorandum asks about Japanese pearl production, alleged smuggling, and expected imports.
subfiles.summary: Goldstone's claims prompt a request for the pearl industry's status and likely export date.

subfiles.title: Draft inquiry to SCAP on the pearl industry
subfiles.about: A State Department officer proposes asking SCAP whether cultured pearls are available and being smuggled.
subfiles.summary: Requests current pearl industry information and an export forecast.

subfiles.title: SCAP account of whaling representatives and tanker conversion
subfiles.about: SCAP details the representatives' duties and the suspension of a third tanker's conversion.
subfiles.summary: Terry and McCracken are designated SCAP representatives, while Japanese inspectors serve on the factory ships. The officers will report on whaling methods and biological data. Conversion of a third tanker has stopped because proposed Bonin Islands operations proved impracticable; a corrected continuation identifies former fisheries chief Fiedler.

subfiles.title: Request for fleet schedule, route, and publicity
subfiles.about: The Department requests sailing dates, route details, and a possible public statement on the expedition.
subfiles.summary: Asks SCAP to address Allied inquiries and adverse publicity.

subfiles.title: Australian aide-mémoire forwarded to Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Department transmits the text of Australia's November 8 aide-mémoire.
subfiles.summary: The reproduced note records Australia's eight understood assurances, provision of an inspector, opposition to future Japanese Antarctic whaling, requests for route information and equipment reparations, and complaint about SCAP's failure to consult the Allied Council.

subfiles.title: Correction to Antarctic whaling flag description
subfiles.about: The Department corrects the code flag specified for the Japanese whaling fleet.
subfiles.summary: The fleet will use SCAJAP flag E, rather than flag O.

subfiles.title: Norwegian note forwarded to Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Department forwards Norway's objection to Japanese whaling and offer of an inspector.
subfiles.summary: Norway objects to a third factory ship and future Japanese Antarctic expeditions. It offers Lieutenant Commander Harald Ostby as an inspector and sets out proposed arrangements for his pay and subsistence.

subfiles.title: Despatch on the International Whaling Conference
subfiles.about: The Political Adviser forwards SCAP and Japanese memoranda concerning conference representation.
subfiles.summary: Encloses proposals concerning a delegate familiar with Japanese whaling.

subfiles.title: Natural Resources Section check sheet on conference representation
subfiles.about: SCAP staff seek advice on whether a Japan-informed representative should attend the Washington conference.
subfiles.summary: Notes Japan's interest in future Antarctic whaling and identifies Fiedler as a possible attendee.

subfiles.title: Japanese request concerning conference delegation
subfiles.about: Japan asks that the U.S. delegation include someone familiar with conditions in its whaling industry.
subfiles.summary: Japan seeks informed representation in decisions affecting its whaling industry.

subfiles.title: Departmental response on conference participation
subfiles.about: The Department explains why it did not invite SCAP participation in the conference.
subfiles.summary: The Department feared that inviting SCAP would prejudice conservation negotiations and imply U.S. support for Japanese whaling in later seasons. It states that Japanese whaling was not discussed at the conference and avoids a commitment on its future.

subfiles.title: Weekly Japanese whaling report: covering despatch
subfiles.about: The Political Adviser forwards three reports for October 20–26 on coastal whaling and Antarctic fleet readiness.
subfiles.summary: Lists reports on catches, products, and fleet status.

subfiles.title: Fleet sailing dates and route
subfiles.about: SCAP reports fleet departures, delays, the planned route, and arrival schedule.
subfiles.summary: Fleet units departed Yokosuka and Nagasaki in mid-November; one catcher grounded and Nisshin Maru needed repairs. The route runs via Mindanao, the Celebes Sea and Lombok Strait, then off western Australia. SCAP expects arrival roughly 30 days after departure.

subfiles.title: Proposed statement on the Antarctic whaling expedition
subfiles.about: SCAP provides text for a U.S. statement explaining the expedition and its controls.
subfiles.summary: The proposed statement gives fleet movements, Allied observer arrangements, route limits, SCAP authority, and anticipated food and oil production. It describes the expedition as a temporary emergency measure and says future Japanese whaling requires Allied decision. The telegram also questions Norway's objections.

subfiles.title: Conference discussions of Japanese whaling
subfiles.about: The Department reports that Japanese whaling was not discussed at the International Whaling Conference.
subfiles.summary: The conference addressed conservation; its papers are enclosed.

subfiles.title: Delayed instructions to whaling fleet representatives
subfiles.about: Tokyo reports delayed receipt of instructions and sends them to SCAP representatives by radio.
subfiles.summary: A mail copy will also be sent to the fleet by ship.

subfiles.title: Corrections to fleet telegrams
subfiles.about: Tokyo corrects vessel descriptions, departure dates, and the fleet's intended latitude.
subfiles.summary: Corrects the proposed statement and earlier route report, including 50 degrees south latitude.

subfiles.title: Weekly Japanese whaling reports: covering despatch
subfiles.about: The Political Adviser forwards coastal and Antarctic fleet reports for October 27–November 2.
subfiles.summary: Lists three Natural Resources Section reports for the week.

subfiles.title: Weekly report of Japanese coastal whaling activities
subfiles.about: The report lists coastal stations, catcher vessels, catches, and vessels under repair.
subfiles.summary: Records 20 whales caught during October 27–November 2.

subfiles.title: Products from Japanese coastal whaling
subfiles.about: The report tabulates oil, meat, blubber, and other products from 20 coastal catches.
subfiles.summary: Lists production by company for October 27–November 2.

subfiles.title: Antarctic whaling fleet weekly status report
subfiles.about: The report records vessel locations and progress on construction, conversion, and repairs.
subfiles.summary: Tables cover Kyokuyo Hogei, Nippon Suisan, and Taiyo Gyogyo vessels. They show several factory ships, carriers, and catchers completed while other vessels remain under construction or repair.

subfiles.title: Duplicate fleet status tables
subfiles.about: A degraded duplicate set of Antarctic fleet status tables follows the clearer copy.
subfiles.summary: Repeats vessel completion and repair information for the October 27–November 2 reporting period.

subfiles.title: Japanese whaling activities: covering despatch
subfiles.about: The Political Adviser forwards a collection of SCAP whaling directives, plans, orders, maps, and correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Lists eighteen enclosures on authorization and control of Japanese whaling.

subfiles.title: War Department inquiry on inspectors and tanker conversion
subfiles.about: Washington requests inspector qualifications and comments on objections to converting a third tanker.
subfiles.summary: Cites British and New Zealand objections ahead of the Whaling Conference.

subfiles.title: Japanese proposal for Antarctic whaling
subfiles.about: Japan requests approval for an Antarctic whaling plan to ease its food shortage.
subfiles.summary: Submits a plan based on existing Japanese whaling experience and equipment.

subfiles.title: Japanese pelagic whaling plans
subfiles.about: Tables propose fleet size, catches, and product yields for the 1946–47 and later seasons.
subfiles.summary: The plans project catches and output of meat, blubber, and oil, with a much larger fleet proposed for 1947–49.

subfiles.title: Recommendation to authorize the 1946–47 expedition
subfiles.from: Hubert G. Schenck, SCAP Natural Resources Section
subfiles.about: SCAP staff recommend authorizing two Japanese factory ships and twelve catchers for Antarctic whaling.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum reviews prewar Japanese whaling, wartime losses, available vessels, expected food and oil output, and international convention requirements. It concludes that the expedition would help relieve shortages and recommends issuing the attached authorization.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1103: authorization of Antarctic whaling
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: SCAP authorizes a bounded 1946–47 Antarctic expedition under vessel, reporting, route, and oil controls.
subfiles.summary: The directive names authorized factory ships, catchers, and carriers and confines operations to a specified Antarctic area and season. It requires radio position and catch reports, a route at least twelve miles from land, return by April 1947, and guarded storage of whale oil. Authorization creates no precedent for future whaling.

subfiles.title: Map of SCAP-authorized whaling area
subfiles.about: A map depicts the authorized Antarctic whaling area and seasonal grounds.
subfiles.summary: Shows geographic limits and preferred whaling months.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1256: change of whaling vessel
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: SCAP permits a replacement catcher vessel for the scheduled operation.
subfiles.summary: Approves Showa Maru No. 10 in place of Takunan Maru No. 8.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1321: representatives with the whaling fleet
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: A second copy appoints Terry and McCracken as SCAP representatives with the fleet.
subfiles.summary: Sets their compliance duties and access to radio facilities.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1321: further duplicate
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Another copy of SCAP's appointment and assistance order for its fleet representatives.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the appointment of Terry and McCracken.

subfiles.title: Instructions for SCAP representatives aboard the fleet
subfiles.to: William M. Terry and David R. McCracken
subfiles.about: SCAP defines the officers' authority, reporting responsibilities, and procedures during the expedition.
subfiles.summary: The officers are to ensure compliance, handle contacts with other nationals, document whaling practices and biological data, and log radio messages. They may resolve urgent directive changes subject to prompt reporting.

subfiles.title: Instructions for SCAP representatives: duplicate
subfiles.to: William M. Terry and David R. McCracken
subfiles.about: A second copy sets out the SCAP representatives' duties aboard the Japanese fleet.
subfiles.summary: Repeats compliance, contact, emergency, statistical, biological, and radio-log instructions.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1329: additional expedition personnel
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: SCAP approves weather observers and a marine engineer but bars media personnel.
subfiles.summary: Authorizes two weather observers and an engineer; denies photographers and correspondents.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1329: duplicate
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: A second copy states SCAP's decision on additional expedition personnel.
subfiles.summary: Repeats approvals for observers and an engineer and rejection of media staff.

subfiles.title: Draft amendment on Antarctic whaling flag
subfiles.about: A draft would require the modified international code flag Easy on fleet vessels.
subfiles.summary: Amends the flag requirement in SCAPIN 1103.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 233: whaling industry directive
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: SCAP requires Japanese whaling to follow international conventions and submit reports.
subfiles.summary: Also directs full use of whale carcasses and marketing of meat as food where possible.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 233: duplicate
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: A second copy sets out SCAP's general whaling industry requirements.
subfiles.summary: Repeats convention, reporting, carcass-use, and food requirements.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1154: added whaling protocols, first copy
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: SCAP adds later international whaling protocols to its earlier directive.
subfiles.summary: Lists supplementary protocols and attached convention texts.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1154: added whaling protocols, duplicate
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: A fuller duplicate adds protocols and directs that treaty reports go to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: The copy lists 1944–46 protocols and attached whaling agreements. It requires all notices and reports due under those agreements to be submitted to SCAP.
